title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree 1st And 2nd Points

questions.question: How does the passage show the close connection between the Qur’an and Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: It shows a two-way connection: the Qur’an supports his prophethood, and his miracles, knowledge, and noble qualities support that the Qur’an is from Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the Qur’an prove about Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: It proves that he is truly a messenger and that his mission is backed by a miraculous book.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, prove about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: He proves that the Qur’an is divine speech, not something made by people.

questions.question: In what areas of human life does the passage say the Qur’an brought major change?
questions.answer: It changed inner life and outer life, including people’s souls, hearts, minds, personal life, social life, and political life.

questions.question: How long does the passage say this influence of the Qur’an has continued?
questions.answer: It says this has continued for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What effect does the passage say the Qur’an has had on very large numbers of people over time?
questions.answer: It has been recited by huge numbers of people and has educated them, improved their character, and purified their inner lives.

questions.question: What different benefits does the passage mention for spirits, intellects, and life?
questions.answer: For spirits it brings growth, for minds it gives guidance and light, and for life it gives true vitality and happiness.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe the Qur’an as unmatched?
questions.answer: Because it brought a deep and lasting transformation in humanity and continues to guide and benefit people in many ways.

questions.question: What example is given to show the Qur’an’s powerful language in early Arabia?
questions.answer: An old famous poem once honored at the Ka‘ba was taken down because it was seen as having no value next to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What can we infer from the story about Labid’s daughter removing her father’s poem?
questions.answer: We can infer that the Qur’an’s language was recognized as far greater than even the best respected Arabic poetry.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the First Point in the passage?
questions.answer: The main idea is that the Qur’an and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, each serve as proof for the truth of the other.

questions.question: Why is Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, called a strong proof for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Because his miracles, prophethood, deep knowledge, and excellent character show that the message he brought is truly from Allah.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an called a miracle connected to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: Because it is one of the greatest signs given to him and confirms the truth of his mission.

questions.question: What kind of revolution does the passage say the Qur’an caused?
questions.answer: It caused a bright, blessed, and truthful transformation in both society and the inner lives of people.

questions.question: Which parts of a person does the passage say were shaped by the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It shaped the soul, heart, spirit, and mind.

questions.question: Which parts of community life does the passage say were shaped by the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It shaped personal life, social life, and political life.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened through the repeated recitation of the Qur’an’s verses?
questions.answer: The recitation kept teaching people, refining them, and cleansing their hearts across many generations.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an’s role for the human mind?
questions.answer: It describes it as a guide and a source of light.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an’s role for human life itself?
questions.answer: It describes it as giving life and happiness.

questions.question: What lesson about the Qur’an’s literary power is taught through the example of the famous poems at the Ka‘ba?
questions.answer: It teaches that the Qur’an’s expression was so superior that even highly honored poetry lost its status beside it.

questions.question: What two things are said to support the truth of Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in the opening part of the passage?
questions.answer: His miracles and the truth of the Qur’an support him.

questions.question: What two things are said to support the truth of the Qur’an in the opening part of the passage?
questions.answer: The Prophet’s miracles and his outstanding knowledge and character support it.

questions.question: What does this mutual support between the Prophet and the Qur’an suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that both come from the same divine source and strongly confirm each other.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the change the Qur’an made in human society?
questions.answer: It describes it as a bright and happy change built on truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an did not only start, but also keep going?
questions.answer: It did not only begin this transformation, but also preserved and continued it over centuries.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened every moment for centuries?
questions.answer: Its verses were continuously being recited by more than a hundred million people.

questions.question: What moral and spiritual effects of this recitation are named in the passage?
questions.answer: People were taught, their character was improved, and their hearts were cleansed.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the Qur’an a marvel and a miracle?
questions.answer: Because of its lasting power to transform people and because no other book is like it.

questions.question: What happened to the reputation of the famous pre-Islamic poems after the coming of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Their importance dropped greatly in comparison with the Qur’an.

questions.question: Why is the statement by Labid’s daughter important in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as an example of people recognizing the Qur’an’s greatness in language and meaning.

questions.question: What is one way the passage proves the Qur’an is from Allah?
questions.answer: It says the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with his signs and virtues, is clear evidence that the Qur’an is divine speech.

questions.question: What is one way the passage proves the Prophet’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an itself, with its miracles and truths, is a sign supporting him.

questions.question: How does the passage present the relationship between miracle and message?
questions.answer: It presents them as joined together, with the book and the messenger each strengthening belief in the other.

questions.question: What kind of human transformation does the passage describe as social?
questions.answer: It describes a change in how people lived together as communities and in how public life was ordered.

questions.question: What kind of human transformation does the passage describe as inner?
questions.answer: It describes a change in the heart, soul, spirit, and thinking of people.

questions.question: What does the long history of recitation show about the Qur’an’s place among people?
questions.answer: It shows that it has remained central, living, and influential across many generations.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to the spirit?
questions.answer: It gives spiritual growth and uplift.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to the intellect?
questions.answer: It gives direction and illumination.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to life as a whole?
questions.answer: It gives real life and joy.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from all these effects?
questions.answer: It concludes that the Qur’an is unique and truly miraculous.

questions.question: In the first point, what is the significance of saying that the Qur’an is a miracle related to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: It means the Qur’an is one of the clearest signs proving his prophethood.

questions.question: In the same point, what is the significance of saying that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is like a miracle related to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It means his life and qualities are strong evidence that the Qur’an is Allah’s word.

questions.question: What features of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are mentioned as evidence?
questions.answer: His miracles, the proofs of his prophethood, and his perfection in knowledge.

questions.question: What broad result did the Qur’an bring to humanity in this world according to the passage?
questions.answer: It brought a bright and truthful transformation to both individuals and societies.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by mentioning the Qur’an’s many verses being read by millions over centuries?
questions.answer: It suggests that its guidance is lasting, widespread, and continually active.

questions.question: What three kinds of improvement in people are directly named?
questions.answer: Teaching them, polishing their character, and cleansing their hearts.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the Qur’an is life for life?
questions.answer: It means the Qur’an gives life its true meaning, strength, and well-being.

questions.question: How does the passage support the claim that the Qur’an has no equal?
questions.answer: It points to its unmatched effect on people’s inner lives, public life, and long-term history.

questions.question: What cultural example is used to show the Qur’an’s excellence in expression?
questions.answer: The example of a prized poem being removed from the Ka‘ba because it was no longer seen as worthy next to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does that example teach about people’s response to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It teaches that even people familiar with the best poetry saw the Qur’an as far above it.

questions.question: What claim does the passage make about the Qur’an and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in relation to each other?
questions.answer: It says each one is a powerful sign confirming the truth of the other.

questions.question: Which side of this relationship points directly to the Qur’an being Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: The Prophet’s miracles, prophethood, and noble excellence point to that.

questions.question: Which side of this relationship points directly to the Prophet’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, with its truths and miraculous nature, points to that.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an changed besides government or public life?
questions.answer: It also changed individual people inside, including their hearts, souls, spirits, and minds.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the Qur’an’s effect was not temporary?
questions.answer: It says the change continued for fourteen centuries through constant recitation and guidance.

questions.question: What role does repeated recitation play in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur’an keeps shaping and improving people across time.

questions.question: What blessing does the passage connect to the intellect?
questions.answer: Clear direction and light.

questions.question: What blessing does the passage connect to the spirit?
questions.answer: Development and rising to a better state.

questions.question: Why would an author include the example of the poem taken down from the Ka‘ba?
questions.answer: To give a real historical picture of how strongly the Qur’an’s language affected people.

questions.question: What overall picture of the Qur’an is built by these three points together?
questions.answer: They present it as divine, life-changing, and unmatched in power and expression.
